sections.title: Compare with -are and -ast
body: To compare two things, add -are and use än: dyr → dyrare än. For the top one of all, add -ast: dyrast. Before a noun with den, det or de, use -aste: den billigaste lunchen.
Use mer and mest with words ending in -isk (praktisk → mer praktisk), words ending in -e (spännande → mer spännande) and long words like intressant. Never use both: say billigare, not mer billigare.

Hindi says Stockholm se bada, and Marathi uses -peksha the same way: the little word sits on the other thing and the adjective does not change. Swedish is like English: the adjective changes (större) and än comes before the other thing: större än Stockholm.
Two words the teacher used for opinions: vänlig means friendly; vanlig means usual. For the taste of food, use god: Maten är godare här. Vad gott! means How tasty!

examples.fi: Det är billigare att åka spårvagn än att ta taxi.

examples.note: Det är + comparative + att … än att … compares two actions.

examples.en: The cheapest lunch costs ten euros.

examples.en: The film is more interesting than the book.

sections.title: Learn the special families
body: Some very common words change shape. Learn all three forms as one chunk: bra–bättre–bäst. Never say mer bra or gammalare.
Count or measure? Things you can count take många–fler–flest: fler bussar. Amounts take mycket–mer–mest: mer kaffe, mer tid. Mindre means smaller or less: mindre tid.

examples.fi: Den här filmen är bättre, men den andra har bäst musik.
examples.en: This film is better, but the other has the best music.

examples.fi: Det finns fler människor i Mumbai, men mer natur i Helsingfors.
examples.en: There are more people in Mumbai, but more nature in Helsinki.
examples.note: People are counted: fler. Nature is an amount: mer.

sections.title: One weekday, last weekday or every week
body: A weekday changes meaning with its small time word. På måndag means the coming Monday. I måndags means last Monday. På måndagar, with plural -ar, means Mondays as a habit.
Look at the verb for a clue: ska or present tense often goes with på måndag, the past (hade, var) with i måndags, and brukar or alltid with på måndagar.
Weekdays start with a small letter in Swedish: måndag, not Måndag. Går usually means goes on foot; åker means travels by bus, tram or train.

examples.note: gick = on foot; åker = by transport.

examples.fi: Måndag, tisdag, onsdag, torsdag, fredag, lördag, söndag.

takeaways: Use -are än to compare two and -ast for the highest; use -aste after den/det/de: den billigaste lunchen.
Use mer/mest with -isk words, -e words and long words such as intressant.
Learn the special families as chunks: bra–bättre–bäst; count with fler, measure with mer.
Use på måndag for the coming day, i måndags for the past day and på måndagar for a habit.
